newsitem.title: AZERBAIJAN: Russians, Chechens, Azeris sign oil transport deal.
newsitem.headline: Russians, Chechens, Azeris sign oil transport deal.

text.p: Azerbaijan, Russia and its breakaway region of Chechnya signed a breakthrough agreement late on Friday to transport Azeri oil via a pipeline crossing their territories.

The agreement, held up for months by bickering between the sides over details, would seem to clear the way for crude output from an $8 billion Western consortium developing offshore Azeri Caspian Sea fields to move through the pipeline to the Russian Black Sea port of Novorosssisk and on to world markets.

The agreement was signed by Russian Fuel and Energy Minister Boris Nemtsov, the president of Chechen state oil company YUNKO Khodzhakhmed Yarikhanov and the president of Azeri state oil company SOCAR.
The consortium, led by British Petroleum plc, wants to begin using the route to transport its oil later this year.

Azeri President Haydar Aliyev had accused Russia's pipeline monopoly Transneft of blocking progress on the deal and warned that Azerbaijan would find other routes to move crude from its new fields onto world markets if neccessary.
